S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled heating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days after learning of it. Incidents involving death, serious injury, evacuation, or an active threat to neighbouring properties must be reported within 24 hours. The manufacturer must notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident indicates a material safety risk or requires action; urgent protective instructions must be sent without delay.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Manufacturers must provide per-model results and test methods to the relevant regulator and provide each model’s failure rate to customers before purchase. Results above 5% require prompt regulator review and a corrective-action plan, including retesting and any interim safeguards the regulator determines necessary. A model must not be automatically barred from sale solely for exceeding 5%; continued sale is subject to regulator oversight and protective measures proportionate to the demonstrated risk. Per-model failure rates need not be published to the general public.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed systems must support remote emergency shut-off by 1 January 2029, subject to safeguards against unauthorized operation and provision for safe local operation. For units already installed when this standard takes effect, manufacturers must provide a compatible retrofit or equivalent mitigation within 6 years, where technically feasible, and notify owners of the available options and any limitations.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard is adopted. The suppression system must be suitable for the battery chemistry and designed not to create additional hazards.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Manufacturers must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, explain the remedy and timeline, and report progress until the recall is complete. A recall requires prompt protective action and corrective measures; following regulator review and verification that the risk is adequately addressed, the model may return to sale.

document.section_notes: S1 is safe with strict reporting and customer notice. S2 is weakened: the 5% failure rate only triggers review/corrective action, and sales never have to stop (indefinite transition), though per-model rates go to customers and not the public. S3 has a 6-year retrofit (acceptable) but new units are due by fixed date 1 Jan 2029, likely beyond the 12-month acceptable window; S4 is acceptable at 36 months; S5 is acceptable with a mandatory 8/100k recall but only 'prompt' notice and no serious-injury clause.
